## Decisions and gates

### Linked model discovery with a partial output cache

- Sources: `last-frontier-map-acceptance:Docs/Plans/2026-10-24-map-acceptance.md`
- Reusable claim: Output discovery enumerates linked model descriptions without reading a partially populated baked model graph; ordinary cached baking retains strict linked-texture validation.
- Decision: ModelInfoBaker owns the discovery boundary and Test_ModelBaker covers both modes; game maps and acceptance policy remain project-owned.
- Promotion gate: Engine-owned linked parent/child fixtures enumerate both outputs with no payload during discovery and reject the missing child during normal cached validation.

### Project bootstrap, staged build, and first launch

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/Architecture.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/BuildAndLaunch.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/Onboarding.md`, `fonline-tla:README.md`, `fonline-tla:CMakeLists.txt`
- Reusable claim: A game consumes an exact Engine revision through staged configure, bake, build, and launch milestones with generated outputs kept non-authoritative.
- Decision: Current Engine guides and examples own the reusable workflow; project presets, binaries, ports, and subconfigs stay external.
- Promotion gate: Engine-owned starter and tutorials pass their declared clean-host lanes.

### Engine submodule update reconciliation

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/DocumentationMaintenance.md`, `fonline-tla:AGENTS.md`
- Reusable claim: An Engine pin change requires a complete incoming-range audit, generated contract comparison, project integration review, and retained safety state until validation completes.
- Decision: The Engine owns reusable reconciliation; each game owns its integration consequences and evidence.
- Promotion gate: The Engine procedure remains executable without either project checkout.

### Generated content ownership and dependency order

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/ContentWorkflow.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/GuiSystem.md`, `last-frontier:LastFrontier.fomain`, `fonline-tla:README.md`, `fonline-tla:AGENTS.md`, `fonline-tla:TLA.fomain`
- Reusable claim: Source metadata, authored resources, generators, baking, and runtime outputs form an ordered ownership graph; generated output is repaired at its source.
- Decision: Reusable ordering is Engine-owned; project generators and concrete outputs retain project ownership.
- Promotion gate: Every generated artifact names its source, generator, validation order, and stale-output signal.

### Script modules, lifecycle, authority, and concurrency

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/Scripts.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/Events.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/Properties.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/Multithreading.md`, `fonline-tla:AGENTS.md`, `fonline-tla:Docs/ScriptStyle.md`
- Reusable claim: Module initialization, callback side, entity covers, async/yield invalidation, events, properties, and generated bindings need explicit ownership and validation.
- Decision: Engine lifecycle and binding mechanics are promoted; game module maps, events, remotes, properties, and lock groups remain project-owned.
- Promotion gate: Claims are tied to Engine callback/export source and focused lifecycle or synchronization tests.

### Script and native nullability

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/Scripts.md`, `fonline-tla:Nullability.md`, `fonline-tla:Tools/NullableEstimate/validate_nullable.py`
- Reusable claim: Nullable script handles and native pointer annotations require one source-backed vocabulary, diagnostics, and analyzer workflow.
- Decision: The Engine guide, compiler diagnostics, and native-boundary checks are normative; TLA migration notes and Last Frontier analyzers remain evidence only.
- Promotion gate: Compiler diagnostics and native-boundary checks enforce the reusable contract; declaration-parity and style analyzers remain explicitly project-owned.

### Native extensions and project-local dependencies

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/NativeExtensions.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/ProjectThirdPartyMaintenance.md`, `fonline-tla:README.md`, `fonline-tla:AGENTS.md`, `fonline-tla:SourceExt`
- Reusable claim: Role-scoped project C++ sources, optional hooks, generated exports, vendored patches, and platform/package guards need explicit source and compatibility ownership.
- Decision: Roles, hooks, and binding rules are Engine-owned; SDK integrations and vendored project libraries stay external.
- Promotion gate: The Engine-owned sample compiles and exercises a role-scoped extension at an exact revision.

### Prototype authoring and validation

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/Prototypes.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/ContentWorkflow.md`, `fonline-tla:README.md`, `fonline-tla:Items`
- Reusable claim: Prototype discovery, identity, inheritance, property applicability, references, migration, and strict values are parser-owned contracts.
- Decision: Grammar and built-in properties are Engine-owned; ids, custom metadata, balance, and directory policy stay project-owned.
- Promotion gate: The generated model derives built-in types and properties from current Engine sources.

### Map authoring, baking, and materialization

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/MapAuthoring.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/ContentWorkflow.md`, `fonline-tla:README.md`, `fonline-tla:Maps`
- Reusable claim: Map sections, placement identity, ownership, mapper round-trip, side-specific baking, and runtime materialization need one parser-backed contract.
- Decision: Format and tool mechanics are Engine-owned; map kits, quests, encounters, and level-design policy stay external. Last Frontier's edge detention bands, four-hex arrival gap, global/local exit separation and preview layouts are project policy; their map/tool/gameplay and owner-visual acceptance remain distinct from reusable format proof.
- Promotion gate: Mapper, baker, loader, and materialization sources agree with generated reference and focused tests.

### Text packs, languages, and runtime lookup

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/Localization.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/ContentWorkflow.md`, `fonline-tla:README.md`, `fonline-tla:Texts/Game.engl.fotxt`
- Reusable claim: Text-pack syntax, duplicate variants, ordered language normalization, prototype text, lookup, and renderer color tags are Engine contracts.
- Decision: Engine format behavior is promoted; language priority, semantic keys, lexems, pack catalogs, and authored text remain project-owned.
- Promotion gate: Current parsers, bakers, script methods, and renderer behavior back every format claim.

### Models, animation timing, and sprite root motion

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/ContentWorkflow.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/CharacterGenerator.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/DocumentationMaintenance.md`, `last-frontier:Resources/CrittersArt/Critters/TEMPLATE_HumanAnimations.fo3d`, `last-frontier:Resources/CrittersArt/Critters/CR_HumanMaleNormal.fo3d`, `last-frontier:Resources/CrittersArt/Critters/VH_Jagger.fo3d`, `last-frontier:Resources/CrittersArt/Critters/VH_Snowmobile.fo3d`, `fonline-tla:Docs/Animation.md`, `fonline-tla:Resources/VanBuren/art/critters/_VBMob.fo3d`, `fonline-tla:Resources/VanBuren/art/critters/_VBWeapon.fo3d`, `fonline-tla:Resources/VanBuren/art/critters/_VBHuman.fo3d`, `fonline-tla:Resources/VanBuren/art/critters/VbDog.fo3d`
- Reusable claim: Current model grammar, named animation tuples, include templates, tuple AnimSpeed, one-step aliases, exact temporary geometry exceptions, typed durations, 2D frame offsets, movement phase, and stop-time offset normalization must be re-derived from Engine bakers and runtime rather than legacy assets or historical documentation names.
- Decision: Engine mechanics are promoted. Last Frontier's named-template composition is current project evidence; its 3D *_RM import boundary does not prove 2D offset values. TLA's bare AnimEqual, model-level Speed, raw_ptr, and LoadAnimation names are explicit legacy migration evidence, not current alias, tuple-speed, pointer, or loader contracts. No current authored 2D root-motion asset was observed in either pinned project snapshot, so project offset values and gait-quality claims stay non-normative.
- Promotion gate: Current parser/baker/runtime sources, focused duration and geometry tests, and visible representative assets replace historical token and implementation-name assumptions.

### Effects, images, sprites, and shader resources

- Sources: `last-frontier:LastFrontier.fomain`, `last-frontier:Resources/Visual/Effects`, `last-frontier:Docs/ContentWorkflow.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/Scripts.md`, `fonline-tla:TLA.fomain`, `fonline-tla:Resources`
- Reusable claim: Effect state/resources, image inputs, FOFRM composition, baked sprites, factories, atlases, and caches require source-backed format and runtime references.

## Owner review requirements

| Owner | Scope | Required evidence | Co-review when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `documentation` | Information architecture, stable document identity, ownership, maintenance policy, and publication routing. | manifest and route impact<br>standalone validation<br>generated site and AI delivery freshness | a domain contract changes<br>locale or publication policy changes<br>a public route is added, replaced, or removed |
| `build-release` | CMake, BuildTools, packages, updater distribution, release automation, and reproducible artifacts. | source or executable parser contract<br>affected build, package, or updater check<br>support and migration disposition | platform capability changes<br>runtime ABI or payload changes<br>credentials, signing, or deployment boundaries are involved |
| `runtime` | Applications, entities, lifecycle, persistence, client/server behavior, and runtime compatibility. | owning source and focused tests<br>lifecycle and failure-path analysis<br>migration or compatibility impact where applicable | script bindings or callbacks change<br>network or persistence contracts change<br>platform host behavior changes |
| `scripting` | AngelScript and Managed C# runtimes, metadata, generated bindings, analyzers, callbacks, properties, events, and script contracts. | source metadata or binding model<br>generated API/reference freshness<br>focused compile or runtime test | runtime lifecycle changes<br>network authority or synchronization changes<br>content metadata or migration changes |
| `content-data` | Configuration, baking, authored formats, resources, maps, movement data, and content validation. | parser, baker, or runtime source<br>generated format model/reference freshness<br>representative bake and validation route | rendered or audible output changes<br>tool authoring behavior changes<br>language or terminology behavior changes |
| `frontend` | Rendering, GUI runtime, media presentation, visual resources, input, and client-visible behavior. | owning render or frontend source<br>focused native/runtime check<br>visible or audible acceptance on every claimed profile | platform backend behavior changes<br>content formats or tools change<br>accessibility or localization presentation changes |
| `networking` | Transport, protocol, connection state, authority, synchronization, and compatibility boundaries. | protocol or synchronization source<br>focused multi-endpoint test<br>compatibility and migration disposition | runtime entities or persistence change<br>script remotes or callbacks change<br>security or deployment boundaries change |
| `tooling` | Mapper, editors, viewers, helper command lines, generated tools, and reusable authoring ergonomics. | tool source or executable parser<br>focused structural or interaction test<br>input, output, persistence, and failure contract | content format behavior changes<br>frontend interaction changes<br>platform packaging or availability changes |
| `platform` | Web, Android, host/target toolchains, platform packaging, device behavior, and backend qualification. | toolchain and target source<br>declared build or smoke lane<br>device or browser evidence for runtime claims | package or release policy changes<br>frontend backend behavior changes<br>runtime host assumptions change |
| `quality` | Tests, diagnostics, analyzers, validation policy, reproducibility, and evidence quality. | reproduction or source-backed invariant<br>focused regression or validator<br>clear pass, failure, and residual-risk signals | the owning domain contract changes<br>a gate is weakened or removed<br>manual evidence is used for a production claim |
| `localization` | English/Russian documentation parity, terminology, source freshness, code integrity, and language-preserving delivery. | canonical English source hash<br>glossary and code-fence parity<br>native-language review and locale link/search checks | technical meaning or identifiers change<br>site routing or navigation changes<br>player-facing terminology overlaps project policy |

## Verification

The normal generator/check validates schema, ownership, disposition rules, Engine targets, and deterministic output. Source verification maps every snapshot to its repository checkout and reads its pinned commit; multiple revisions may share a checkout without changing HEAD. Dirty or newer files cannot supply missing pinned sources. Unsupported repositories, missing commits and missing sources are errors.

```bash
python BuildTools/docs_external_evidence.py --check
python BuildTools/docs_external_evidence.py --check --verify-sources --last-frontier-root ../ --tla-root Workspace/fonline-tla-audit
```
